title: Largest Number After Mutating Substring
summary: Given a string representing a large integer and a mapping array that transforms each digit, determine the largest possible integer by optionally mutating a single substring of the input string according to the transformation rules.
statement: Given a string representing a large integer and a mapping array that transforms each digit, determine the largest possible integer by optionally mutating a single substring of the input string according to the transformation rules.
constraints: change has exactly ten replacement digits from 0 through 9.
You may choose at most one contiguous substring and must replace every chosen digit d with change[d].
hints: The first increased digit dominates all later positions; after mutation begins, equal replacements may bridge to later gains but a decrease must end the substring.
Skip until change[d]>d, then replace while change[d]>=d and stop permanently at the first decrease.
Scan digits with a started flag: improve starts; equality continues only after start; decrease after start breaks.

Starting at the earliest improvement maximizes the first changed position. Continuing through nondecreases cannot hurt, while crossing a decrease would make the first such position smaller regardless of later gains.
editorial: Starting at the earliest improvement maximizes the first changed position. Continuing through nondecreases cannot hurt, while crossing a decrease would make the first such position smaller regardless of later gains.

tests.explanation: Mutating the first two digits gives 832, the largest possible result.
